Environment-Stability Workflow: Reliable and Transportable Feature Sets

stabl_environment_stability.Rd

Fits STABL separately in each environment and aggregates per-feature selection frequencies by their minimum across environments: a feature is only as reliable as its weakest environment. This delivers ICP-inspired stability-across-environments (Peters et al.) as a predictive selection heuristic — without causal assumptions, without an environment-variable requirement beyond labels, and without new dependencies.

Usage

stabl_environment_stability(x, y, environments, lambda_grid = "auto",
                            random_state = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A matrix or data.frame of features (samples in rows).

y

Named outcome vector; sample IDs must match rownames(x).

environments

Factor or character vector with one label per sample (batch, cohort, site, ...). Must contain at least two non-empty levels and no NA.

lambda_grid

Passed to stabl_fit(); either "auto" (per-environment grids) or an explicit grid. Note that "auto" grids reach the saturated small-lambda regime, which makes max-over-lambda scores lenient; explicit top-heavy grids discriminate better.

random_state

Optional integer seed; per-environment seeds are derived deterministically from it via the package's hashed multi-stream derivation (the same pattern as stabl_fit() and the multiomic workflows; changed from the pre-1.0 consecutive random_state + i derivation, F-019).

...

Additional arguments forwarded to stabl_fit() in every environment.

Value

A list of class "stabl_env_stability" with elements env_fits (named list of per-environment "stabl_fit" objects), env_scores (features x environments matrix of max-over-lambda selection frequencies), min_scores (minimum across environments), mean_scores, environments (levels used), pairwise_adjusted_similarity (environment x environment similarity of selected sets), and call.

Details

Environment labels may be batch, cohort, or site identifiers. Group integrity within each per-environment fit is preserved by passing environment labels through the usual grouped-bootstrap machinery. The minimum-aggregation rule is deliberately conservative: features whose signal is environment-specific receive a low minimum score. This is a stability heuristic, not a causal-effect estimate and not an FDR guarantee.

See also

stabl_fit(), get_importances(), adjusted_similarity().

Examples

set.seed(1L)
n <- 90L
env <- factor(rep(c("batchA", "batchB", "batchC"), each = n / 3))
x <- matrix(rnorm(n * 6), n, 6,
            dimnames = list(paste0("s", seq_len(n)), paste0("f", 1:6)))
y <- setNames(1.2 * x[, "f1"] + 0.8 * x[, "f2"] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5),
              rownames(x))
res <- stabl_environment_stability(
  x, y, env,
  lambda_grid   = data.frame(lambda = c(0.6, 0.4, 0.25)),
  n_bootstraps  = 10L,
  hard_threshold = 0.5,
  random_state  = 1L
)
res$min_scores                      # transportability summary
#>  f1  f2  f3  f4  f5  f6 
#> 1.0 1.0 0.0 0.2 0.0 0.0 
get_min_scores(res)                 # same, via accessor
#>  f1  f2  f3  f4  f5  f6 
#> 1.0 1.0 0.0 0.2 0.0 0.0
